reason: Alar regions are patches of enlarged cells at the leaf base in mosses. They are regions made of many cells, not one alar cell. They also lack a clear PO class. Reject rather than map to one cell.
An alar group is a cluster of cells. The target is a single cell type, so the meaning is lost.
An alar area is a region of the leaf base, not a cell. It is not the same as alar cell.
Flowerhead is the usual word for a capitulum in the Asteraceae. The PO lexicon already lists 'head' as a synonym.
'Flower head' is a capitulum in daisy-like plants. In other families it can mean a dense spike or umbel, so apply it only where the head is a true capitulum.
The plural of flowerhead, with the same meaning.
A brood body is a gemma-like vegetative propagule. The word is also used for bulbils and plantlets in flowering plants, and those are not gemmae.
The plural of the previous rule, with the same limit.
A culm sheath is borne on the culm, as in bamboo. It is not a leaf sheath, although it is a modified leaf. No exact PO class was found. Do not map it to leaf sheath.
The plural of the previous rule. A culm sheath is not a leaf sheath.
A median vein is the midvein only when the part is a leaf or leaflet. On other parts, such as a sepal or bract, it would not be a leaf midvein.
'Médiane' is an adjective meaning median. Alone, it does not name a midvein and can mean median lobe, median tooth, median sepal and more.
A pseudostyle is a false style, such as the beak on a fruit or a style-like structure. It is not a true style, so mapping it to style gives it a wrong meaning.
The plural of the previous rule. A pseudostyle is not a style.
Perula, perulae and perule are the botanical words for bud scales, and the lexicon has bud scale as a synonym.
The Latin plural of perula. It means bud scales.
This is an English or French variant of perula. It means bud scale.
Primary divisions of a frond are pinnae. The word is used for other things in other contexts, such as the primary division of a calyx or an inflorescence.
The plural of the previous rule, with the same limit.
This is the French form of the previous rule. It holds for fronds and compound leaves only.
A valve of a capsule is a valve of a fruit, so fruit valve fits.
The plural of capsule valve, with the same meaning.
This is the same as capsule valves, in a different word order.

A false panicle, or pseudopanicle, is an inflorescence that looks like a panicle but is built differently. The target 'inflorescence' is true but loses the panicle-like shape. Use inflorescence with a shape quality, or reject.
This is the French form of false panicle. The same loss of meaning applies.
A spatheate compound panicle is an inflorescence with a spathe and a compound branching pattern. The target keeps neither feature.
Propagula covers many kinds of propagule, such as bulbils, stolons and plantlets. It is a gemma only in bryophytes.
'Asexual propagula' names any vegetative propagule. It is a gemma only in bryophytes.
A needle is a leaf in conifers. In other plants, 'needle' can describe a spine, a crystal (raphide) or a hair.
The plural of needle, with the same limit.
A needle leaf is a leaf. The PO lexicon lists 'needle-like leaf' as a synonym of vascular leaf.
An intersecondary vein is a specific vein class between secondary veins. Leaf lamina vein is true but loses the class. Reject unless a specific vein class exists.
This is the English form of the previous rule. The same loss of the vein class applies.
Leaf blade is a synonym of leaf lamina, so a leaf blade lobe is a leaf lamina lobe.
The plural of leaf blade lobe, with the same meaning.
A lamina lobe is a leaf lamina lobe.
'Phyllaryllary' is a typing error for 'phyllary'. Phyllary is a synonym of involucral bract, so the target is right, but the key is garbled. Use the key 'phyllary' instead.
The singular of propagula. It is a gemma only in bryophytes.
A bisexual flower has both stamens and pistils. The target 'flower' drops this sexual condition. Use flower with a quality such as bisexual.
A hermaphrodite flower is bisexual. The target 'flower' loses that.
A perfect flower is bisexual. The target 'flower' loses that.
The symbol ☿ means hermaphrodite. The target 'flower' loses that.
A vegetative part is any non-reproductive part, such as leaves, stems and roots. It is broader than the vegetative shoot system, which excludes roots.
The plural of vegetative part. It has the same problem.
A female inflorescence is pistillate only in plants with separate sexes. The PO lexicon lists it as a synonym, so the rule is mostly right.
The plural of female inflorescence, a listed synonym of pistillate inflorescence.
This is the French form of female inflorescence.
The phrase means the inflorescences of the female flowers, which are pistillate inflorescences.
An aristate scale is a scale with an awn, here a pappus scale. 'Aristate' is a shape quality, so the key names a quality plus a part. Map the part to pappus element and the quality to aristate.
The plural of aristate scale. 'Aristate' should be a quality, not part of the bearer.
